newsitem.title: INDIA: India tax reliefs seen aiding two cement firms.
newsitem.headline: India tax reliefs seen aiding two cement firms.

text.p: The Indian government's move to exempt firms with units in backward areas from a minimum alternate tax will benefit cement maker Gujarat Ambuja Cements Ltd, Jardine Fleming Broking said on Thursday.
The new tax or MAT, was imposed on "zero tax" paying firms in the July 22 budget. On Wednesday, the finance minister said he was exempting firms located in backward areas from MAT.
Jardine Fleming said the firm's plant in the northern state of Himachal Pradesh was a notified backward area.

"This will reduce Gujarat Ambuja's effective tax rate to around 10 percent for 1996/97 and below 10 percent for 1997/98. Associated Cement Companies, which has a two million plant in Himachal Pradesh, will benefit as well," it said.
Jardine analyst Pradeep Mahtani said cables firm Sterlite Industries, which has some plants in backward areas, would be another beneficiary of these relief measures.
